failure_summary.description: Calls omitted explicit filters or selectors and used values with incorrect casing or API-specific slug formatting.
Agents added a loosely related result or an overlapping endpoint instead of limiting calls to requested outcomes.
A call object repeated a parameter-collection key, preventing the requested optional parameter from being represented reliably.

patch.reasoning: The batch most often shows failures in carrying explicit request details into the right tool-specific parameters and using their canonical value formats. A focused parameter audit can address those errors without encouraging guessed values. A concise call-pruning and serialization check covers the extra calls and duplicate key while avoiding a broader checklist that has been ineffective in prior steps.

edits.content:
## Map request details to tool parameters
- For each requested result, map every explicit qualifier—such as a date boundary, locale, page, or filter—to the corresponding parameter documented for that endpoint. Do not omit an explicitly requested setting merely because the endpoint has a default.
- Use the endpoint's documented parameter names and value representation, including required casing, slug, code, token, and data type. Do not assume a display name can be converted into an API value by an intuitive spelling change. Use only values grounded in the request or tool documentation; preserve free-text values unless the documentation specifies normalization.

## Avoid redundant calls and validate structure
- Call only for requested outcomes. If one endpoint directly covers a requested result, do not add another endpoint for the same or overlapping check, and do not add unrelated results.
- Before submitting, check that each call has the required interface structure and exactly one entry for each parameter collection; remove duplicate keys.
